transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-08-02
- Start time: 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Meridian CTO), Leah Park (ML Eng), Omar Aziz (Security), Nina Ho (PM)

Summary:
Redwood team runs discovery to understand Meridian AI's model selection requirements across Hosted/Dedicated/Private options. Key topics: preferred open models, context length needs (long-context documents, 50k+ tokens), multilingual support (primary EN + ES/FR/JP support), tool-calling and function/tool orchestration, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security (VPC, KMS, SOC2), and pilot/benchmark next steps. Meridian leans toward a Dedicated pilot but wants hosted benchmarks first.

Topics:
- Current stack and usage patterns
- Target latency and throughput
- Context length and KV/prefix caching needs
- Multilingual and rare-language support
- Tool-calling / function calling / structured outputs
- Security/compliance and deployment mode preferences
- Pilot/benchmark plan and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey thanks everyone for joining i see folks are here, um, we'll do quick intros. i'm jordan i'm the AE on the account. priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Carlos Mendes: hey, carlos here, cto at meridian. thanks for taking the time.
[00:14] Leah Park: leah, ml eng, i'm the day to day on model integration.
[00:17] Omar Aziz: omar, security and compliance.
[00:20] Nina Ho: nina, product, hi all.
[00:22] Priya Natarajan: great thanks, i'll kick off with a few questions about your current infra and then we can talk models. sound good?
[00:28] Carlos Mendes: sounds good. high level — we ingest long research documents and internal knowledge bases. Our main product does doc understanding, qa, and multi-turn summarization. we need models that handle long context, ideally up to 50k tokens, sometimes more for batch jobs.
[00:45] Priya Natarajan: ok 50k — good to know. are these mostly single-doc context or do you concat many docs into one prompt?
[00:52] Leah Park: it's a mix. interactive sessions concat a subset, and offline jobs we stitch entire corpora so sequence length matters for cost. we also do multilingual support — english primary, but spanish and french frequently, some japanese.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: and what's your current stack — self-host, cloud, any LLM providers?
[01:09] Carlos Mendes: currently using an in-house setup with a mix of open checkpoints, we evaluated openai and a few cloud managed endpoints, but cost spiked as usage grew. we have some on prem infra for sensitive data.
[01:20] Priya Natarajan: got it. so thinking through redwood options: Hosted gives fastest time to value for evaluation, Dedicated gives reserved capacity and predictable latency, and Private gives you full control in a VPC or on-prem. for 50k contexts you'll want models and kernel/serving optimizations — and caching.
[01:36] Omar Aziz: security is a big one — we need SSO, SAML, audit logs, KMS, and data residency info. SOC2 type II and iso are required for our procurement.
[01:46] Jordan Lee: yes we can share the security pack. we support SSO, audit logs, KMS integrations, and have SOC2/ISO docs — i'll send those after.
[01:54] Nina Ho: timeline wise we want a pilot in q3, ideally start with hosted benchmark then move to dedicated if cost and latency look good.
[02:02] Priya Natarajan: that's a common approach. quick question on model preferences — are you leaning toward any open models? we've seen folks evaluate llama 3 series, mistral foundation models, mosaic/mosaic-ml, and some specialized long-context models (e.g., longform variants).
[02:20] Leah Park: i've been testing llama 3 and a longform-mistral fork. for single-token quality we like llama 3 but it becomes heavy on memory for 50k, the longform variants handle memory better. also we need tool-calling — structured function outputs for downstream pipelines.
[02:39] Priya Natarajan: ok yes tool-calling is supported across our runtime; function-calling semantics sometimes differ across model families — we'll map that out. for really long context we recommend models that support sliding KV cache and sparsity-aware kernels — our runtime can enable kv prefix caching and chunked attention for some model variants.
[02:59] Carlos Mendes: when you say "some model variants" — do you mean Redwood maintains optimized kernels for specific checkpoints?
[03:06] Priya Natarajan: yes we do kernel selection and compilation per model — we optimize per-architecture. for instance if you pick a Mistral derivative we route to the best kernels and we also have quantized execution paths to reduce memory. that affects latency and cost.
[03:22] Leah Park: how about multilingual quality — we have Spanish/French user base. do you bench multilingual LLMs?
[03:27] Priya Natarajan: we have multilingual performance profiles in the model catalog; some open models have better non-English coverage. we can include multilingual prompts in the benchmark.
[03:35] Jordan Lee: pricing question — rough order: hosted per-token + embeddings, dedicated reserved capacity monthly. we'll provide a pricing sheet after we scope expected qps and context lengths.
[03:45] Carlos Mendes: our qps is modest — maybe 5-10 rps peak for interactive, and heavy batch nightly jobs. latency target for interactive is sub-600ms median for small prompts, and up to 2s acceptable for long-context but cost should be reasonable.
[04:03] Priya Natarajan: sub-600ms median is possible on Dedicated with smaller models or optimized variants; for 50k context the long attention increases latency, but we can use prefix caching for interactive sessions to reduce repeated compute. also model distillation/quantization can bring cost down at a small quality tradeoff.
[04:26] Omar Aziz: about data retention and logs — do you persist prompts or full transcripts in hosted mode? our policy prefers ephemeral by default and optional retention for debug with encryption.
[04:36] Jordan Lee: default hosted doesn't persist raw customer prompts beyond retention window unless you opt in — for Dedicated/Private you control retention and storage. we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest.
[04:49] Nina Ho: tool-calling — we need structured JSON outputs to feed downstream pipelines. do models guarantee stable schema or do you provide wrappers?
[04:58] Priya Natarajan: function/tool calling is supported; we also provide a lightweight schema enforcement layer in the console and SDK that validates model outputs and retries or uses hallucination suppression heuristics. it's not magic but helps.
[05:13] Leah Park: any gotchas with function-calling across models? e.g., some open models disregard function hints more often?
[05:19] Priya Natarajan: yes model alignment differs — we'll include that in the benchmark and measure schema adherence. it's one of the metrics we track.
[05:28] Carlos Mendes: ok so for the pilot we'd want: 1) multilingual QA + summarization 2) long-context 50k batch jobs 3) interactive sessions with caching and tool-calling.
[05:38] Jordan Lee: that's a great scope. our recommended next step is a hosted benchmark with a few model families (llama 3 variants, mistral-long, mosaic longform) to measure cost, latency, and schema adherence. if results meet your SLOs, we can scope a Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity and custom kernel optimizations.
[05:57] Omar Aziz: procurement will need SOC2/ISO and a short answers doc. can you provide that?
[06:02] Jordan Lee: yes i'll send the security pack and a short questionnaire.
[06:06] Nina Ho: what about timeline for kernel-level optimizations — can that be done before a Dedicated pilot?
[06:11] Priya Natarajan: we can do some optimizations in our hosted environment and show gains, but Dedicated gives you full control over instance types and kernel tuning. some model conversions for long context take engineer cycles — we'll estimate effort in the benchmark results.
[06:27] Leah Park: question: do you support tool-chaining — like model calls that trigger external reasoning or database lookups?
[06:32] Priya Natarajan: yes, we support tool orchestration via function calls + orchestration hooks, and we can stream partial outputs during long runs so UX doesn't block.
[06:41] Carlos Mendes: any limitations on concurrency for long-context jobs on hosted?
[06:45] Jordan Lee: hosted has soft concurrency limits to protect multi-tenant infra; Dedicated removes that with reserved GPUs. for heavy nightly batches Dedicated is more predictable cost wise.
[06:56] Nina Ho: are there recommended quantization profiles for long-context models? we've seen 4-bit quantization helps memory but sometimes hurts multilingual quality.
[07:05] Priya Natarajan: correct; we recommend mixed strategies — per-model profiles we've created (e.g. q4_gold, q3_long) which balance memory and quality. we'll include suggested quant configs in the benchmark.
[07:20] Carlos Mendes: can you run the benchmark on our sample dataset? it includes research PDFs and transcripts.
[07:24] Priya Natarajan: yes we'll need a sanitized sample — if there's PII we'll route through your VPC or use anonymized data. for hosted benchmark we'd prefer anonymized set; for Dedicated/Private we can test on your raw corpus in VPC.
[07:39] Omar Aziz: is there an NDA or data processing addendum we should sign before sharing raw data?
[07:43] Jordan Lee: we can exchange an NDA and DPA; i'll attach those.
[07:47] Leah Park: about evaluation metrics — can we track semantic similarity, rouge/bleu for summarization, hallucination rate for tool-calling outputs?
[07:57] Priya Natarajan: yes we can plug in your eval harness or use ours; we'll report BLEU/ROUGE/EM and also hallucination/error rates for function outputs.
[08:06] Jordan Lee: i'm going to propose concrete next steps — run a 2-week hosted benchmark with 3 model families, include multilingual test set, function-calling test, and 50k batch test. after that review results and decide on Dedicated pilot.
[08:22] Nina Ho: timeline-wise that's perfect for our q3 goal.
[08:26] Carlos Mendes: can you also include per-token cost estimate for each model family?
[08:30] Jordan Lee: yes we'll estimate per-token cost and cost per query for your typical sessions.
[08:34] Omar Aziz: one more question about logs and audit access for Dedicated — can we push logs to our SIEM?
[08:40] Priya Natarajan: yes Dedicated supports log forwarding to customer SIEM and structured audit logs.
[08:45] Leah Park: curious about SDKs — we use python and go.
[08:48] Jordan Lee: we have python, node, go SDKs; streaming support is available.
[08:52] Carlos Mendes: ok any red flags? nothing immediate but we need to see benchmarks for long-context reliability.
[08:59] Priya Natarajan: understood. we'll include stress tests and measurement for tail latency.
[09:05] Nina Ho: regarding rollout — if pilot succeeds how fast can we move to Dedicated?
[09:09] Jordan Lee: usually 4-8 weeks depending on capacity commitments and contract; if you need faster we can prioritize.
[09:15] Carlos Mendes: and pricing models for Dedicated — flat monthly for reserved GPUs plus usage for bursts?
[09:20] Jordan Lee: correct, reserved plus burst; details in the pricing sheet.
[09:24] Leah Park: about model updates — do you pin model versions? we need reproducibility for audits.
[09:29] Priya Natarajan: you can pin model version and we support rollbacks and canary deploys. we also keep model artifacts and hash metadata.
[09:36] Omar Aziz: encryption in transit and at rest details?
[09:38] Jordan Lee: TLS in transit, KMS-backed encryption at rest, customer-managed keys are supported in Dedicated/Private.
[09:45] Nina Ho: last item — demo request: can we get a short demo of function-calling/schema enforcement?
[09:50] Priya Natarajan: yes we can do a 30-45 minute demo in the follow-up call.
[09:55] Jordan Lee: recap — we'll send security docs + NDA, pricing for hosted vs dedicated, benchmark plan and sample prompts, and schedule benchmark and follow up.
[10:07] Carlos Mendes: sounds good. thanks everyone. we'll prep data and compliance questions.
[10:12] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up with the attachments and dates.

End of transcript.
